microscopic_coupling_only.caveat: This baseline uses the bare α_0 with surface compactness only. It yields ~10⁻²⁴, confirming that the measured η is not produced by the microscopic coupling alone. η is an emergent observable response coefficient.

standard_scalar_tensor.caveat: Standard scalar-tensor Nordtvedt formula. The ~8.8× enhancement (using the Cassini upper-bound α_0 ≲ 3×10⁻³) indicates that η absorbs additional contributions from the TEP screening mechanism beyond bare scalar-tensor physics.

volumetric_tep.caveat: Phenomenological TEP prediction from integrated density profiles (step_026). The ~3–5× residual is absorbed into PREM simplification, (ρ/ρ_T)³ exponent uncertainty, ρ_T = 20 ± 8 g/cm³ uncertainty, and the upper-bound nature of the Cassini α_0 constraint.

conclusion: η = -3.1773e-04 is the LLR observable response coefficient. Three baselines are presented: (1) microscopic-coupling-only η = α_0² Δ(Φ²) = 4.3427e-24 yields an enhancement of 7.32e+19×, confirming that η is emergent and not produced by bare α_0 alone; (2) standard scalar-tensor η ≈ 4α_0² = 3.6000e-05 yields an enhancement of 8.8×, indicating that η absorbs TEP-specific screening contributions beyond standard scalar-tensor physics; (3) the phenomenological volumetric TEP model η ≈ -α_0 Δ⟨(ρ/ρ_T)³⟩ = -9.6594e-05 yields an enhancement of 3.3×, with the residual ~3–5× absorbed into model uncertainties. The measured η is much smaller than cross-domain κ values (η/κ_Cep ~ -3.03e-10), consistent with LLR being in a more screened Solar System regime.
